issues.description: Patch does three things. Should be three patches.
issues.detail: This diff bundles (a) the Risk Radar feature + category selector, (b) a wholesale 'Threat Score' -> 'Prowler ThreatScore' rename across unrelated files (risk-plot, threat-score component), and (c) a horizontal-bar-chart width/percentage computation refactor. These are independent concerns with independent risk profiles. The rename alone touches files that have nothing to do with the radar. Split into: (1) categories util + radar component + findings filter, (2) ThreatScore wording change, (3) bar-chart percentage refactor. A maintainer six months from now bisecting a bar-chart regression should not have to read a category-selector diff.

issues.description: getCategoryLabel silently changes behavior for unknown IDs.
issues.detail: The old adapter had an explicit CATEGORY_LABELS map: 'iam' -> 'IAM', 'trustboundaries' -> 'Trust Boundaries', 'forensics-ready' -> 'Forensics Ready'. The new heuristic in lib/categories.ts handles 'iam' (<=3 chars -> 'IAM') and 'forensics-ready' ('Forensics Ready'), but 'trustboundaries' now becomes 'Trustboundaries' instead of 'Trust Boundaries'. That is a visible regression caused by deleting the explicit map without auditing every key it covered. Either keep the explicit table as the source of truth and use heuristics only as fallback, or add the known-bad cases to SPECIAL_CASES with a test. Don't replace a working lookup with a clever heuristic and call it equivalent.

issues.description: SPECIAL_CASES is dead code committed as a placeholder.
issues.detail: An empty Record with a 'add entries here if needed' comment is exactly the gratuitous abstraction the maintainer should refuse. Either populate it with the cases the old explicit map covered (trustboundaries, etc.) or delete the dictionary and add it when the first real case shows up. Shipping empty scaffolding is hostile to the next reader: they have to figure out whether it's used.

issues.description: displayPercentage logic in HorizontalBarChart is a special case that could be general.
issues.detail: The new code introduces calculatedWidth and displayPercentage as two separate branches off the same item.percentage fallback. They diverge only in whether they round and whether they default to total or maxValue. Pull a single helper `computePercentages(item, total, maxValue)` returning {width, display}, and the branching collapses. Also: Math.max(...data.map(...)) is recomputed inside the .map for every item; hoist maxValue (and total if it's computed downstream) above the .map so it isn't recomputed per-row. Minor, but bad taste in a hot render path.

issues.description: SEVERITY_ORDER now has duplicate value 4 for Informational and Info.
issues.detail: Adding `Info: 4` next to `Informational: 4` papers over an upstream inconsistency about how that severity is named. Two keys with the same numeric value is a smell — somewhere a producer emits 'Info' and somewhere else emits 'Informational', and rather than fix that, we're tolerating both here. Fine as a tactical fix, but leave a one-line comment naming where the divergent producer is so the next person can delete one of these. Otherwise this duplication metastasizes.

issues.description: CategorySelector handles 'empty string' value that the component never emits.
issues.detail: `if (value === '' || value === 'all')` — the SelectItem values are 'all' and the category IDs. Empty string is never passed in by this component. Either it's defensive-programming-by-superstition (delete the empty-string branch) or it's a real path from the underlying Select primitive emitting '' on clear (in which case document it). Right now it reads like noise.

issues.description: Removing category__in from DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES without explanation in commit message.
issues.detail: The diff removes the 'category__in' badge from DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES but the PR description doesn't mention it. Either category badges are now produced by a different path (in which case say so in the commit) or this is an inadvertent regression where selecting categories no longer shows an active filter badge. State the why in the commit message — that's what commit messages are for.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The radar feature itself is reasonable and the categories utility is the right direction — pulling label formatting out of the adapter into lib/ is correct. But this is three patches submitted as one (radar feature, ThreatScore rename, bar-chart percentage refactor), and the new getCategoryLabel silently regresses at least one known label ('trustboundaries' -> 'Trustboundaries' instead of 'Trust Boundaries') because the explicit lookup table was deleted in favor of a heuristic without auditing every key it covered. The empty SPECIAL_CASES dictionary is gratuitous scaffolding. Split the patch, restore label fidelity (either keep the explicit map as primary or populate SPECIAL_CASES and add a test), and tighten the bar-chart helper before this lands.
